People looking at this serum are probably debating between The Inkey List (TIL) and The Ordinary (TO) Niacinamide 10% + Zinc 1%. I?™ve tried both, so I wanted to compare/contrast between the two and offer my own experience. I have oily skin with visible sebaceous filaments, and I?™m prone to blackheads and the occasional whitehead.Let?™s start with the ingredient breakdown. Both serums contain a 10% concentration of niacinamide by volume. Both contain xanthan gum (a stabilizer that also helps oil and water mix), and both contain VERY hydrating antimicrobial alcohols that can be good for your skin - TO uses pentylene glycol, while TIL uses butylene glycol (?œalcohol??in this sense refers to the chemical composition of these compounds - while it also fits the definition, we?™re not dousing our faces in vodka here). This is where the similarities end. TO contains 1% Zinc (in a salt form, pyrrolidone carboxylic acid) which, in addition to regulating sebum production, also acts as a natural humectant, which means it helps your skin retain some of its natural moisture. TIL does NOT contain zinc whatsoever. It does, however, contain Squalane and Hyaluronic acid, as well as an ingredient called ?œLeuconostoc/Radish Root Ferment Filtrate,??which is still being studied for its uses as a natural preservative because it has small amounts of salicylic acid. The data is still a bit inconclusive on that end, but butylene glycol acts as an antimicrobial agent anyway so it?™s still shelf-stable.I used one full bottle of TO?™s serum, applied nightly. I?™ve been using TIL?™s serum for 5 months and am currently using it. It?™s HG. While I DO have shiny, oily skin, I don?™t get a ton of whiteheads or cystic acne - that might be why I broke out from TO. The zinc might be too strong for me. I find TIL?™s to be much more hydrating. My skin loves hyaluronic acid and TO does not contain any.People with heavier breakouts would probably love TO, but for oily skin and mild acne? This is perfect.

The first ingredients are rose water which are the key hydrators. Rosa Damascena (fancy for rose water) is actually an old herbal medicinal that has proven anti-inflammatory benefits meaning it reduces irritated skin and eczema. It also contains squalene. Squalene protects the skin by acting as an antioxidant and prevents moisture loss. It is a moisturizing agent that replenishes fatty acids to protect and build your skin layer, I can?™t rave enough about this nourishing ingredient. Finally, the serum contains a blend of oils like rosehip camelina and rose flower which are safe skin softening ingredients. After messing around on where this product belonged in my skincare routine, I found myself enjoying it. This product will give you the glass skin effect because of its unique ingredient list. Not only that but its hydrating enough to use alone in those warm nights. One thing I didn?™t like is the perfume part, I am slowly trying to reduce perfumes in my ingredients as they have become to irritate my skin. That being said, I would definitely still recommend this!

It?™s just - consistently good at making my skin look better.I wouldn?™t recommend this product for anyone with dry skin because of the alcohol in it. Alcohol isn?™t the kiss of death with skincare products -- the reason so many companies put it in their products is that it makes the active ingredients absorb better into your skin! However, it does that by weakening your moisture barrier so that ingredients can penetrate better. For that reason, you shouldn?™t use more than one product with alcohol in it -- the effect of multiple applications of alcohol to the skin is much worse than a single application per day. People with dry skin should avoid products containing alcohol, as they can exacerbate dryness. Those of us with normal or oily/combination skin are probably safe to use one (1) alcohol-based active skincare product per day. For me, the benefits of the First Care Activating Serum outweigh the potential negatives. I?™ve repurchased like 5x and will continue to do so.

It?™s just - consistently good at making my skin look better.I wouldn?™t recommend this product for anyone with dry skin because of the alcohol in it. Alcohol isn?™t the kiss of death with skincare products -- the reason so many companies put it in their products is that it makes the active ingredients absorb better into your skin! However, it does that by weakening your moisture barrier so that ingredients can penetrate better. For that reason, you shouldn?™t use more than one product with alcohol in it -- the effect of multiple applications of alcohol to the skin is much worse than a single application per day. People with dry skin should avoid products containing alcohol, as they can exacerbate dryness. Those of us with normal or oily/combination skin are probably safe to use one (1) alcohol-based active skincare product per day. For me, the benefits of the First Care Activating Serum outweigh the potential negatives. I?™ve repurchased like 5x and will continue to do so.

Alcohol isn?™t the kiss of death with skincare products -- the reason so many companies put it in their products is that it makes the active ingredients absorb better into your skin! However, it does that by weakening your moisture barrier so that ingredients can penetrate better. For that reason, you shouldn?™t use more than one product with alcohol in it -- the effect of multiple applications of alcohol to the skin is much worse than a single application per day. People with dry skin should avoid products containing alcohol, as they can exacerbate dryness. Those of us with normal or oily/combination skin are probably safe to use one (1) alcohol-based active skincare product per day. It doesn?™t layer well with a lot of products (essentially every drunk elephant product hates this). HOWEVER. However. However. I was gifted this a week ago. I got this while on vacation in Florida because I left my rose and witch hazel based toner at home. I took a trip to Sephora specifically to purchase this toner with high expectations due to my almost obsession with Fresh products. As toner was the last remaining item I do not use on my face with the Fresh label, I was gleefully expecting greatness. What I found:1. Packaging. As other reviewers have pointed out, unlike most of the moisturizing products made by Fresh, the bottle is plastic, not glass. I sort of shrugged, because even though I hate plastic, I understand why a company would use it to package. Yet it does take away from the Fresh experience and also makes the product inside seem cheaper. I don?™t store it in a warm place, so I hope that nothing leaches into the product from the plastic bottle.2. Effectiveness. It is not as effective as witch hazel based toners. To me, a toner should be not just moisturizing, but also cleansing and firming. This left a little plumper feel and the scent is wonderful, but it lacks the extra firming and pore reduction of witch hazel.3. The spray nozzle. I don?™t bother to use this. After using water-based refreshing sprays before, the feature doesn?™t make sense to me. It?™s not exactly a travel-sized bottle. I?™m not going to be carting it around in an evening bag. Why is this feature necessary? Maybe to make a lackluster product more appealing. I?™m not entirely sure. If it came with a smaller travel bottle that was more portable, I would be more inclined to carry it and spray it on myself in public, but carrying what essentially feels like a tube-shaped weapon in my purse does not appeal to me in the least.4. The cost. I clearly spend money on my beauty regime. Other than organic produce and overpriced yoga pants from Lululemon, lotions and eye creams are where the majority of my hard earned money is spent. I have no problem shelling out ungodly amounts of cash for beauty products that at least make me feeeeel better about aging and free radicals (I do recognize this is a construct of the society in which I live and has little to do with the actual effectiveness of most products.) This product fails miserably at this. When I can purchase a product at my local organic co-op with organic rose and witch hazel for a fraction of the price of this ?œtoner,??the marketing is clearly failing. If this were marketed exclusively as a refreshing spray with a smaller, glass bottle, I admit, I would probably have given it 5 stars. It?™s refreshing scent and the idea of rose (I used to use the C.O. Bigelow rose water based products as a teen and twenty-something religiously) has always appealed to me.
